PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
BOARD MEMORANDUM (draft for General Counsel review, due March 12, 2025; board meeting March 18, 2025)
TO: Board of Directors, Greenleaf Industries, Inc.  FROM: Marcus Chen, In-House Regulatory Counsel (via Diana Whitmore, General Counsel)
RE: SEC 2023 Beneficial Ownership Amendments (Release No. 33-11253; 34-98704) and Our Current Shareholder Situation

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
- Thornfield's Schedule 13D was TIMELY. Counting business days from the January 14 crossing, with Monday January 20 (Martin Luther King Jr. Day) excluded, the fifth business day was January 22, the day Thornfield filed. Investor Relations' "one day late" count wrongly counts the holiday; we should not allege a violation.
- The real exposures are different: (a) a possible undisclosed Thornfield-Ridgeview "group"; (b) Thornfield's cash-settled swaps (2.3 million reference shares), which are disclosed but not counted; (c) the risk that Apex's Schedule 13G passive status is compromised; (d) a monitoring system that cannot see swaps; and (e) a calendar gap: the nomination window closes before our March 18 meeting.
- No one is near the 15% rights-plan trigger. The Thornfield-Ridgeview stake is about 9.26%; they would need about 10.6 million more shares.
- Recommended now: a brief telephonic board session before the nomination window closes (March 13-14), a records and bylaw check, and informal groundwork on the pill. Details in Section 6.

2. WHAT CHANGED (plain language)
2.1 Schedule 13D (activists, holders over 5% with control intent). The initial filing deadline went from 10 calendar days to 5 business days after crossing 5%. Amendments for any material change are now due within 2 business days (previously "promptly"). A change of 1% or more of the class is deemed material (Rule 13d-2(a)); smaller changes, including a new plan to nominate directors or a change in group membership, can also be material. These 13D changes were effective February 5, 2024.
2.2 Schedule 13G (passive holders). Compliance date September 30, 2024.
- Passive investors (Rule 13d-1(c)): initial filing within 5 business days of crossing 5%; amendment within 2 business days of exceeding 10% and of each 5% change thereafter.
- Qualified institutional investors (QIIs, Rule 13d-1(b)) and exempt investors: initial filing within 45 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which they cross 5%. Quarterly (rather than annual) amendments within 45 days after quarter-end for any material change. Crossing 10%, or moving 5% after that, requires filing within 5 business days AFTER THE END OF THE MONTH in which it occurred (not 5 business days from the event).
2.3 Group guidance. The SEC did NOT adopt its proposed rewrite of Rule 13d-5 (including the "tipper-tippee" concept), and did not adopt a safe harbor. It instead gave interpretive guidance under Section 13(d)(3): a group needs an agreement, arrangement or understanding to act together for acquiring, holding, voting or disposing of shares, but it can be informal and inferred from circumstances (not a written contract); mere communication, even about a possible approach to management, is not by itself a group; coordinated action (for example, jointly pursuing an agenda or parallel trading in concert) can be.
2.4 Cash-settled derivatives. The SEC did NOT adopt the proposed Rule 13d-3(e), so cash-settled swaps do not automatically count as beneficial ownership. Item 6 of Schedule 13D now expressly requires disclosure of cash-settled derivatives. Whether a swap counts remains a facts-and-circumstances question (for example, if the holder has or shares voting or investment power, including by arrangement with the counterparty, or uses the swap to evade the rules under Rule 13d-3(b)).
2.5 Structured data and conversion. All 13D/13G filings must be in the SEC's custom XML format from December 18, 2024. A 13G filer that loses eligibility must now file a 13D within 5 business days (previously 10 days). The "cooling off" bar on voting and buying more shares, running from the change in purpose until 10 days after the 13D is filed, is long-standing, not new.
Source-document errors to correct: Stonebridge's Feb. 20 letter and Nov. 2023 bulletin (and our Monitoring Manual) variously state a 10-day conversion deadline, a "new" cooling-off period, an amended Rule 13d-5 safe harbor, a 'promptly' 13D amendment standard (bulletin), 5 business days from the event for QII 10% crossings, and September 30, 2024 for the 13D deadline. Ask Stonebridge to confirm in writing.

3. THORNFIELD CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LP
3.1 Timeliness: compliant. Crossing: Tuesday January 14, 2025. Business days: Jan 15, 16, 17, [Jan 20 federal holiday], 21, 22. Deadline: January 22. Filed January 22. Action: confirm the EDGAR acceptance timestamp (before 10 p.m. ET) from the filing header. 3.2 Content issues worth raising with Stonebridge:
- Swaps. Item 6 discloses cash-settled swaps referencing 2.3 million shares (about 1.24% of the class; $38.5 million notional at $16.74; expiries June-December 2025). Excluded from the 10.1 million shares (5.46%). If counted, Thornfield holds about 12.4 million shares (6.70%). The filing says swaps are settled only in cash and that Thornfield has no right to vote or acquire the reference shares. That is a standard position. We have no evidence yet that it is wrong, but swap counterparties commonly hedge by buying shares. 
- Cover page: Item 6 says Row 12 is checked, but the excerpt shows it and Row 2 (group) unchecked; confirm against EDGAR.
- Amendments. IR reports 400,000-600,000 more shares in February (0.22%-0.32%), taking Thornfield to roughly 10.5-10.7 million shares (5.7%-5.8%). Under 1% (1.85 million shares), such purchases alone are not presumptively material. But any change in plans (a nomination, a campaign, group membership, new swaps) requires a 13D/A within 2 business days. The IR memo's "as of February 28" data is dated February 26 and mixes figures; the current count is unverified.

4. RIDGEVIEW AND APEX
4.1 Ridgeview (about 7.03 million shares, 3.80%). Alone it has no filing duty. IR's indicators: parallel buying starting in early December, same solicitor (Copperfield, reportedly), similar analyst questions. Each is circumstantial; hearsay in part; none shows an agreement. Under the SEC guidance, a group requires an understanding; shared advisers and parallel trading raise an inference but are not conclusive, and independent funds may legitimately pursue the same thesis.
If a group exists: combined 17.13 million shares = 9.26% (10.1 + 7.03; ÷ 185). With swaps (if counted): 19.43 million = 10.50%. Consequences: (a) the group must report on Schedule 13D (Thornfield's cover and Item 6 deny any understanding; Exhibit B shows no joint filing), so the disclosure would be deficient; (b) timing: the group may have crossed 5% before January 14 (both began buying in early December), which would make the 13D late as a group filing; trading records are needed. 
Proposed approach: no public accusation; Stonebridge to evaluate a letter to both funds and informal SEC contact. Groups require proof of an agreement (Morales v. Quintel, 249 F.3d 115 (2d Cir. 2001)).
4.2 Apex (15.17 million shares, 8.20%; 13G/A filed Feb. 12, 2025, within the quarterly deadline of Feb. 14). Risk factor only. The only evidence is one second-hand report that an Apex portfolio manager attended a February 5 dinner hosted by Mr. Voss and was an active participant. Attendance alone does not mean Apex has a control purpose, and the SEC guidance protects ordinary shareholder discussions.
4.3 Staff guidance after the Stonebridge letter's analysis. On February 11, 2025, the SEC Division of Corporation Finance issued C&DI 103.12 (and revised related items): a shareholder who goes beyond discussing views and applies pressure on management to implement specific changes (for example, adopting specific governance measures or board changes), or conditions voting on them, may be seen as having a control purpose and so lose 13G eligibility.
If Apex's certification were compromised: Apex must file a 13D within 5 business days and may not vote or buy more shares from the date of the change until 10 days after filing. That matters: 8.2% is our largest block. It could also make Apex a possible member of a group; combined with Thornfield-Ridgeview that would be 32.3 million shares (17.46%), above the pill trigger, but this is speculative and rests on no confirmed fact. Do not make approaches that would pressure Apex's engagement choices; our contact with Apex should be ordinary governance engagement.

5. MONITORING (VantagePoint) - gaps
- It does not capture cash-settled derivatives; Thornfield's swaps (1.24%) are invisible to alerts. Mitigation: read Item 6 of every 13D/13D-A; seek swap data via our financial adviser.
- Alerts cover direct holdings and filed data only; unfiled groups and late filers are invisible; the parallel-accumulation algorithm gives false positives.
- The Manual is out of date (deadlines, QII and passive rules); review times should shrink given 2-business-day amendments. Verify XML parsing is live.
- Calendar quarterly 13G windows (next: May 15, 2025).

6. DEFENSIVE CONSIDERATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
6.1 Advance notice timing. Our materials compute the window from the expected 2025 meeting date (June 11), giving February 11 to March 13. But the bylaw (Art. II, Sec. 12, as described by IR) runs from the ANNIVERSARY of the prior meeting, June 12, 2024. On that reading the window is February 12 to March 14, 2025. We have not been given the bylaw text; the Corporate Secretary must confirm the exact formula (and any provision for a meeting date moved by more than 30 days). Until then, treat the window as open through Friday, March 14, and treat notices as possibly arriving through that date. Also, under SEC Rule 14a-19 (universal proxy), a dissident must give notice at least 60 days before the anniversary (about April 13, 2025) and solicit 67% of voting power. The March 18 meeting is after the bylaw window closes. Recommendation: a short telephonic board session or lead independent director briefing before March 13; instruct the Corporate Secretary and Stonebridge to log, date-stamp and review any notice for bylaw compliance (form, disclosure and ownership requirements) within days.
6.2 Rights plan (pill). Facts: 185 million shares; 15% = 27.75 million shares. Current positions: Thornfield 10.1 million (5.46%); Ridgeview 7.03 million (3.80%); group 17.13 million (9.26%). Shares needed: 10.62 million (5.74% of class). If swaps are counted by the plan's definition (many plans include derivatives): group 19.43 million (10.50%); needs 8.32 million (4.50%). With Apex (speculative): 32.3 million, 17.46%, already over.
Documents conflict on whether the plan is adopted but dormant or only a form; a shelf plan needs a fresh board resolution. Legal framework (assuming Delaware, unconfirmed): enhanced scrutiny under Unocal Corp. v. Mesa Petroleum Co., 493 A.2d 946 (Del. 1985) (reasonable threat, proportionate response); pills valid in principle (Moran v. Household Int'l, 500 A.2d 1346 (Del. 1985)); In re Williams Cos. S'holder Litig. (Del. Ch. 2021), aff'd (Del. 2021), struck a pill with a low trigger and broad group/derivative provisions. Cite-check before reliance. Assessment: on present facts (activist at about 9% as a possible group, no creeping control, no nomination yet), adopting a pill now would be hard to justify as proportionate and could invite a challenge and ISS/Glass Lewis criticism; the 15% trigger is conventional. Lowering to 10% or adding derivative or group language would heighten risk. Recommendation: do not activate now; prepare to adopt quickly if triggers occur (a group filing above about 12%, evidence of a control-oriented group including Apex, a derivative-based stealth build, or acceleration of buying); document the board's process and have Stonebridge pre-draft resolutions and a fact record; keep Pinnacle on standby (manual 4.3).
6.3 Actions. (1) By March 13: telephonic board briefing; GC confirms the bylaw window. (2) Verify the EDGAR timestamp and the full 13D (Rows 2 and 12, Exhibit C). (3) Stonebridge: written rule corrections and group-evidence analysis. (4) Financial adviser for swap and stock-loan intelligence; review Item 6 routinely. (5) Apex: ordinary-course engagement only. (6) Update the Manual and VantagePoint. (7) Pre-draft pill resolutions; confirm incorporation state and plan terms.
Limits: facts rest on unverified IR intelligence; 13D excerpt only; bylaw and plan text not supplied; the SEC release was not directly fetched (network blocks), so confirm rule points against 88 Fed. Reg. 76896.
